records.query: Need bronchoscopy findings detailing subglottic and tracheobronchial mucosal injury, including carbon deposits or soot, to confirm the extent of the e-cigarette airway burn and guide airway management.

Need bronchoscopy findings to directly assess the extent and severity of airway burn and rule out distal tracheobronchial injury, along with carboxyhemoglobin level to evaluate potential inhalation injury from the e-cigarette.

Need CT of the neck and chest to assess the depth of thermal injury and exclude concurrent traumatic airway disruption from the fall, along with blood cultures and epiglottic cultures to definitively rule out infectious epiglottitis, given the diffuse supraglottic edema and lack of prodrome.
records.text:
Computed tomographic scan showed glottic and supraglottic swelling with no evidence of fractures.
Direct laryngoscopy showed diffuse edema and sloughing of pharyngeal and supraglottic mucosa, most severe in the epiglottis

bindings.label: Patient presented with stridor, increased work of breathing, and supplemental oxygen requirement

A man presented to the emergency department on transfer from an outside hospital after falling with an e-cigarette in his mouth several hours earlier; he did not remember the exact cause of the fall and believed he may have lost consciousness
Physical examination in the ED showed diffuse supraglottic edema most severe in the epiglottis, arytenoids, and aryepiglottic folds, which obstructed a view of the true vocal cords
CT shows glottic and supraglottic swelling without fractures
Direct laryngoscopy shows diffuse pharyngeal and supraglottic mucosal edema with sloughing, most severe in the epiglottis
